name: Samrat Choudhary
role: Chief minister of Bihar (2026–); former deputy chief minister and state BJP leader
summary: Choudhary promotes welfare delivery, industrial investment and employment alongside stronger policing and continued liquor prohibition. He supports a uniform civil code and a cow-slaughter ban, has endorsed investigations framed around love jihad, and defends caste reservations through constitutional channels.

notes:
Read full interviews from 2024, 2025 and September 2026, examined earlier religious campaign pledges and current policing controversies, and checked every one of the 490 statements. Policies explicitly defended in his interviews count as his; his party’s national manifesto and other leaders’ policies do not automatically count. Caste reservations are not assumed to be racial preferences, and proportional representation of castes is not proportional allocation of legislative seats by party vote. Investigating alleged coercive conversion does not establish a general ban on voluntary conversion or interfaith marriage. Religious observance and support for one temple do not establish scriptural law, clerical rule or a religious test for citizenship. The police inquiry is recorded alongside the encounter controversy; tough policing is not converted into approval of killing suspected drug offenders without trial. Demolition of alleged encroachments, and his promise to protect lawful owners, do not establish a general doctrine of fundamental property rights. Employment targets combining private and public work are not universal state job guarantees. Flood-control engineering does not itself establish a climate-change policy. The absence of direct positions on most world, ecology and technology statements remains unknown; no inference from party, caste or family.

Merged with an independent claude-sonnet-5-5 audit: 4 answers taken from it, 10 agreed, 1 conflicts settled by the integrator.

claude-sonnet-5-5 notes: Independent second pass built from long interviews and speeches of his own (Hindi auto-captions read directly, plus 2022-2023 Indian Express interviews) rather than the Organiser and Idea Exchange pieces the first audit used. Themes searched: economy (industrial, welfare, subsidies, budget), liberty (prohibition, drugs, police, encounters), government (dynasty, democracy, courts, panchayat reservation), culture, technology and nuclear power, world (Farakka and the Bangladesh water treaty, Operation Sindoor, infiltrators), ecology, society. Cattle slaughter, conversion law, UCC, hate speech and caste reservation could not be settled from the new sources: on the UCC he said only that Bihar will decide after talks with coalition allies (Panchayat AajTak, Sept 2026), which is not a stated position either way. Caste reservation is not answered on the race-based statements; the Bihar caste survey he called incomplete, which is not a position on any statement. Translations from Hindi are mine, and auto-captions carry no speaker labels, so each passage was used only where the chief minister is plainly the one answering. Policies count as his where he drove or defended them in his own words; the Centre's and allies' positions do not. 'Encounter' record: more than a dozen police encounters under his government (ETV Bharat), balanced by his own stated rejection of direct encounters and the judicial inquiry he ordered, so extrajudicial-killing stays 0 at low.
